lines.text: Morning, Grace. Can you hear me okay? I've got the little bar showing but it's not moving when I talk.
Morning. Yes, I can hear you fine. You're a bit quiet, maybe, but it's clear.
Let me push the mic up. Is that better?
Better, yes. That's louder.
Hello, hello. Sorry, am I in? I got the spinning circle for about a minute there.
You're in, Wei Ling. We can see you and hear you.
Good. I'm on the laptop today, not the desktop, so if the picture freezes that's why.
Mm-hm, no problem. Jonas should be coming in any second, I saw his name pop up in the lobby.
Hi all. Sorry, I'm here, I think. Can you see me? I've got a blank square on my side.
We can see you, Jonas. Your camera's on.
Oh, right, it just came up. Sorry. I was fighting with the sharing settings in this thing, it keeps asking me to allow something.
Every time. It's always the same pop-up, you click allow and it asks again.
Yes, exactly that. Anyway, good morning.
Good morning. Has everyone got a coffee? I'm on my second and it's not even a proper start yet.
Tea for me. I've been in since early, so I'm already ahead of myself.
I've got one going cold next to me, I always make it and then forget it.
Same. Mine's somewhere under the paperwork.
Right, well, let's not wait on the coffee. Is everyone able to see the papers? Ravi, you sent the pack round, did people get it?
I did, it should be the report and the one-page summary. Wei Ling, Jonas, you have both?
I have both. I've got the summary open on my other screen.
Got them. I haven't read every page, I'll be honest, but I've seen the summary.
That's fine, the summary is the main thing. Okay, I think we're all here, so let's get going.
Agenda: tender result, stage 3 approval, furniture, the IT install and the landlord approval.
Ravi, start with the tender result please.
The contractor tender closed on the twentieth of November and we only got two bids, we were hoping for at least four.
Two out of four. Hm. So half of what you wanted.
Yes, about half. We had hoped for more interest than that, to be fair.
Two bids is thin. Does procurement accept that as competitive?
Procurement said two is the minimum they accept, so we're compliant, but it's a problem for value for money.
Right. So it passes the rule but it doesn't feel great.
That's how I'd put it. It passes, and I'm not comfortable pretending it's a strong field.
Can I ask, when you say a problem for value for money, is that because we can't compare enough prices?
Yes, that's the main part of it. With only two, you can't really tell where the middle of the market is.
Mm-hm, okay. That makes sense.
With two you've basically got one comparison. Either one's cheap or the other's dear, you can't say which.
That's the worry, yes. Ravi, what were the numbers?
Kemlite Builders came in at three hundred and ten thousand, the other bid was three hundred and forty five.
Sorry, say the second one again. Three hundred and forty-five?
Three hundred and forty-five thousand, yes. And Kemlite at three hundred and ten.
Okay. I just wanted to be sure I had them the right way round. Kemlite is the lower one.
Kemlite is the lower one, correct.
So the lower bid is also the one that's, what, the better design? Or is that a separate question?
That's a separate question, and it's in the end stage report. I'd rather take it when we get to the approval, if that's okay.
Sure, sure. I'm jumping ahead. Go on.
No, it's a fair thing to ask. But let's hold it for a minute. Before we move on, I want to go back to the two bids.
When I read the summary I thought, is there anything we can do about only getting two? Or is that just where we are now?
The tender has closed, so the bids are what they are. What I can tell you is what procurement said, that two is accepted.
Mm. I'm not trying to reopen it, I just want to be sure we're not nodding something through because it's convenient.
No, I understand. That's why I flagged the value for money point up front, I didn't want it buried.
I'd say that's fair. You did say it plainly in the summary.
Thanks. I'd rather say it plainly.
Do we know whether the two bids were priced on the same basis? I mean, are they like for like?
I'd want to check the detail before I answered that properly. I don't want to say from memory and get it wrong.
Fair enough. I'm only asking because the gap looks tidy, but a tidy gap can hide differences.
Mm-hm. Though Wei Ling mentioned something about the design, didn't you? I saw a note.
I did, yes, it's about what each design included. I can say it when we're on the approval, like Ravi said.
Okay, good. Let's do that then, so we don't go round twice.
Can I just say one more thing on the tender? Just that I'm happy to answer questions on it after the meeting too.
Noted. Jonas, are you happy with where we are on the tender?
Yes. It's thin, we've said that, and it's compliant, we've said that. I don't have more on it.
Right. Anyone else on the tender result? No? Okay.
That brings us to the end stage report and stage three.
The end stage report recommends we award to Kemlite and move into stage three, construction.
Right. And that's the recommendation in black and white, the lower bid.
Yes. That's what the report says on the front page.
This is where I was going before. Wei Ling, you said there was a point about the design?
From the user side the Kemlite design met all our must-haves, the other one dropped the second meeting room.
Ah. So the second meeting room, that's the difference.
That's the difference I was thinking of, yes. For us, it's a must-have, so it matters.
Just so I'm clear. The other bid, the higher one, left out the second meeting room.
That's what I said, yes. The other design dropped it.
Okay. So it's not just that Kemlite is lower. The other one is higher and also gives you less.
From the user side, that's how I see it, yes.
And that was reflected in the end stage report, that's part of why we recommended Kemlite.
Okay, that helps me a lot. It means the two bids aren't as hard to choose between as I'd feared.
I was thinking that too. With only two bids I was worried we were choosing between nothing, but this is a clearer choice.
Mm-hm. I'd still keep the value for money point on record, but it isn't muddying the choice.
Right, and I don't think the user group would want the other one anyway, not without the room.
No, I wouldn't either. Okay.
Any other questions before I put this to the board? Jonas?
No, I'm fine. I'm happy for it to go to the decision.
Wei Ling?
No, none from me. The must-haves are covered, that was my main concern.
Ravi, anything you want to add before I say it?
Only that the report is the basis for it, so if anyone wants the detail it's all in there.
Good. Right, let me say it so it's on the record.
Okay, the board approves stage three and the award to Kemlite Builders at three hundred and ten thousand.
Agreed from me.
Agreed, yes.
Thanks, I'll issue the letter of award tomorrow.
Good. Thank you, Ravi.
Congratulations, I suppose, to everyone. It's the moment it becomes real.
Ha, yes. Stage three, construction. It sounds more serious now.
It does a bit. Feels like we've been at the planning part for a long time.
Mm. Okay, let's keep moving, we've got a few more items.
Furniture. Wei Ling?
The workstation supplier is quoting ten weeks lead time now, it used to be six.
Sorry, ten? I hadn't seen that, I had six in my head.
Yes, ten now. It came through to me, I think, after the pack went out, so it's not in the report.
Okay, that's why. I'd have put it in. Six to ten, that's a big move.
Did they say why it's changed? Or is it just a number on the quote?
I don't have a reason to give you. It's what they're quoting, that's all I can say for sure.
Right. So we don't know if it's going to settle back or stay there.
No, we don't. That's the bit that worries me.
If that holds, there's a real chance the desks arrive after the move-in date.
Hold on, say that again. After the move-in date, the desks?
The desks, yes. If it's ten weeks and it stays ten weeks.
Right. That would be a poor start. People moving in with nowhere to sit.
Mm. Not great, no.
I'd say it's an if, though. Wei Ling said if that holds. It's not certain.
Yes, I agree, it's not certain. But I said a real chance, and I meant it. I didn't want to wave it away.
No, no, I'm not waving it away. I just want us to keep it as what it is, a chance and not a fact.
I think that's fair on both sides. It's a real chance, it isn't certain.
Is there any sense of when we'd know whether it holds?
I can't say that. I don't have anything from them on it.
Okay. Just thinking aloud.
Can we order before the design is fully signed?
We can order the standard desks now and only the meeting room tables later.
Ah, okay. So it's just the meeting room tables that have to wait.
Yes, the standard desks don't depend on that, as far as I can see. The meeting room tables do.
And that fits, because the second meeting room is part of what we've just approved. So that piece is the one still being worked through.
Right, that's the connection I was making.
So the tables come later and the desks come now. That splits it nicely.
It does. Though I don't want to rush into a decision on it here, I'd rather hear a bit more first.
Agreed. Do you want me to take that away and come back to it, or is it something you want to settle in this meeting?
Let's talk it through for a minute and see where we land. Wei Ling, you've said you can order the standard desks now. Is that your preference?
It's what's possible. I'd like us to use it, given the lead time, but I know it's a board question.
Mm-hm. I can see why you'd want to.
Right. Okay. Anything from anyone else on the furniture before we go on?
Just a small one. Wei Ling, could you send me the quote, so I have the ten weeks in writing?
Yes, I can do that. I'll forward it, it's in my inbox.
Good. Thanks. Let's take a breath there, and then I'd like us to move on.
IT install. Jonas.
The network install in January needs the central IT team, and they're also committed to another project that month.
Right. So just so I've got it straight, it's not your people who are the constraint, it's central IT.
Yes, that's it. We can do our part, but we can't do it on our own. We need them there with us.
Sorry, can I check something? When you say they're committed to another project, is that already confirmed on their side, or is it more that they've said they're busy?
What I've been told is that they're committed. I haven't seen their plan, so I can't tell you how firm it is. I'm just passing on what I heard.
Okay. Mm-hm. I just wanted to know whether it was a hard thing or a soft thing.
Honestly, I don't know. That's part of why I wanted it on the agenda today.
Fair enough. Go on, Jonas, you were about to say what it means for the install.
So our install can only happen if central IT gives us the second and third week of January.
The second and third week. Both of them, together?
Both. That's the window we need. One week on its own doesn't work for us.
Right, right. I'm just looking at the programme here. Yeah, that matches what I have. January, second and third week, and the network goes in then.
And is that something you've already asked them for, or is this the first time it's being said out loud?
We've talked to them, but nothing's been agreed. So at the moment it's what we need, not what we've got.
Okay. That's quite a difference.
It is. That's why I'm stating it so plainly. If they can't give us those two weeks, then we can't do it. I don't want anyone thinking it's more flexible than it is.
No, that's useful. I'd rather hear it plainly now than find out later.
Mm. Can I ask, is it the whole of central IT we're talking about, or particular people in it?
I only deal with the team as a whole. I couldn't tell you who inside it. I'd be guessing.
Okay, no, that's fine. I wasn't looking for names, I just wanted to understand the shape of it.
Can I go back one step? You said the other project is in January too. Is it the same weeks, do we know?
All I was told is January. I don't have more than that. So I can't say whether it overlaps exactly or only partly.
Which is a bit awkward, because if it only partly overlaps, there might be some room in it. But we don't know.
Right. We don't know. I'm not going to pretend there's room when I haven't seen it.
No, fair. I'm only thinking aloud.
I think that's what I'm getting at too. We're guessing at the other project, so it's hard to say how worried to be.
I'd say take it seriously, but we don't need to panic over it yet. We've got a clear statement of what's needed. Two weeks, second and third of January, from central IT.
Second and third week, yes. Sorry, not the dates, the weeks.
Sorry, yes, weeks. Thank you.
Can I just say, it's good that it's come up now and not in January.
Agreed. That's the only upside.
Ha. Yes, small mercies.
Right. Is there anything else on the IT side before I say what I'm going to do about it? Ravi?
No, I think that's all of it from me. It's the one dependency on that side, and it's central IT.
From the user side, I don't have anything more either. I just want to be sure we're all describing it the same way.
Let me say it once more, then. The install happens only if central IT gives us those two weeks. That's the whole thing.
Yes. Okay. That's clear, thank you.
I'll raise it with the IT director at the leadership meeting on Thursday.
Thanks, Grace. That would help a lot.
Yes, thank you. That's the right level for it.
Will that be a quick conversation, do you think, or is it something that needs a longer slot?
I can't say. It depends on how the meeting goes. I'll put it to them and we'll see what they say.
Sure. I'm not pushing, I was just curious.
And I'm happy to leave it with you from here. I don't think there's more I can add on it until we hear back.
Same. Until there's an answer, we're just carrying it as it is.
Okay. Good. That's enough on IT. Anything anyone wants to go back to before we move on?
No, I'm fine. I think we've said it from every angle.
Yes, fine from me.
Nothing from me.
And the landlord approval of works.
Our schedule is built on the landlord approving the works by the thirteenth of December.
Sorry, can I check, is that the thirteenth as in the approval has to be in hand by then, not that they start looking at it then?
Yes. Approved by the thirteenth. That's the point the schedule is built on.
Okay. Good, because those are quite different things, and I wanted to be sure which one we were talking about.
So where are we with them now? Have they said anything at all?
They haven't said no, they just haven't replied, so for now we keep assuming the thirteenth.
Right. So it's silence, basically.
Silence, yes. Not a refusal, not an approval. Nothing.
And that's the only thing we've had from them? No hint either way?
Nothing either way. That's why I say we keep assuming the thirteenth. There's no reason on the table to assume anything else.
Mm-hm. Can I ask, from our side, if it did move, would we hear about it from you first?
You'd hear it from me, yes. But at the moment there's nothing to hear. It's the thirteenth until somebody tells us otherwise.
Okay, good. I just like to know where the information comes from.
I suppose what I'm wondering is how worried we should be about the silence. Is it normal for them to take a while?
I don't want to say it's normal or not normal, because I don't have a view on that. All I can tell you is they haven't replied and they haven't said no.
Okay. That's fair. I don't want you to guess.
Mm. And the thirteenth, that's the date everything else hangs off, is that right?
The schedule is built on it, yes. That's all I'd say. I'm not going to describe what happens if it moves, because I'd be making it up.
No, that's sensible. I'm not asking you to.
I'd say the same from my end. I don't want to speculate about what a different date would do.
Can I just say, I'm a bit uncomfortable that it's the same kind of situation as the IT one? We're waiting on somebody else, and we don't really know how firm anything is.

I see why you'd say that. They are similar in one way, we depend on someone outside the team. But they're not the same. With IT we've been told what the problem is. With the landlord we've been told nothing.
Right, yes. One is a known constraint and the other's a blank.
That's a good way to put it.
I'd go along with that. Though I'd point out both come back to the same thing, which is that we can't control either one directly.
True. We can only make it clear what we need and when.
Exactly.
Sorry, one more. When you say they haven't replied, Ravi, is it that they've been asked and haven't come back, or that they haven't been asked?
They've been asked. It's with them. They haven't come back.
Okay. Thanks. I just wanted to be sure it wasn't sitting on our side.
No, it's with them.
Mm. Good.
Okay. Is there anything else anyone wants to ask Ravi on this before I say where I'd like to leave it?
Not from me.
No. I think I've got the picture. Approval by the thirteenth is what we're assuming, and we've had no answer.
That's it exactly.
Okay, keep chasing them, and tell me early if it slips.
Understood.
Fine by me.
Yes, fine.

Right. I think that's us for those two items. So, quick wrap-up. On IT, the need is clear and I'll take it to the IT director on Thursday. On the landlord, we keep going on the thirteenth and keep chasing.
That's how I have it too.
Yes, same. Thanks, everyone.
Thanks, Grace. Thanks all.
Thank you. We'll leave it there. Goodbye, everyone.
Bye, all.
Bye.
Bye.
